en: The Banaue Rice Terraces act as a giant inclined plane, reducing the effort needed for farmers to climb the steep mountains of Ifugao.
The deep treads on a jeepney tire increase friction with the road, preventing the vehicle from slipping during heavy rainy days.
Galileo famously dropped two different masses from the Leaning Tower of Pisa to prove gravity pulls all objects down at the same rate.
The massive electromagnet on a scrap yard crane picks up and moves heavy pieces of magnetic iron easily.
The Bakun Hydroelectric Plant in Benguet generates electricity by using the kinetic energy of flowing water to spin large turbines.
Fireflies in Loboc, Bohol produce visible light through bioluminescence, a chemical reaction inside their abdomens that does not generate heat.
The Philippine golden-capped fruit bat uses echolocation, emitting high-pitched sound waves that bounce off objects to navigate in the dark.
The Tiwi Geothermal Power Plant in Albay harnesses the Earth's internal heat to boil water and produce steam for generating electricity.
Water at the top of Pagsanjan Falls possesses gravitational potential energy that converts into kinetic energy as it rushes downward.
The Archimedes screw is a simple machine featuring a helical surface inside a pipe that lifts water to higher elevations.
The streamlined, pointed nose of the MRT-3 train in Manila reduces air friction, allowing it to move faster and use less energy.
A magnetic compass used by Ferdinand Magellan points north because its magnetized needle aligns with the Earth's invisible magnetic field.
